definition: Legal protection from liability for entities that comply with specified safety standards or regulatory requirements, incentivizing proactive compliance.
rationale_for_coinage: Safetyists see safe harbor as an incentive for voluntary safety compliance. Accelerationists see it as necessary protection for good-faith innovators. Skeptics see it as a corporate shield allowing minimal compliance while avoiding accountability. The bare term conceals these divergent evaluations of the mechanism.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Performative compliance is the failure mode; safe harbor is the intended incentive. Skeptics argue safe harbor enables performative compliance.

contested_aspects: Whether safe harbors incentivize genuine safety or minimal checkbox compliance
Whether safe harbor provisions can be gamed by sophisticated actors
Whether the standards defining safe harbor are set by the right parties
